tagline: China's late-night food capital — Mao's home province's neon city, famous for stinky tofu, a river-island park and snack streets that run till dawn.
overview: Changsha is the capital of Hunan — the province that gave China Chairman Mao and its most aggressive cuisine. The city wears both proudly: a giant statue of young Mao anchors Orange Isle in the Xiang River, and the night markets keep the chili flowing until sunrise.

Chinese foodies rate Changsha's snack streets among the country's best — stinky tofu, crayfish and sugar-oil rice cakes along Pozi Street and Taiping Old Street. The serious side lives at the Hunan Museum, where the Mawangdui tombs hold a 2,100-year-old marquise preserved so well her skin was still soft.

Speed's 2025 China tour ended here amid chaotic crowds — and produced the viral story of the 'braised goose uncle,' a vendor who followed Speed across the trip and became a national celebrity overnight.
